To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

shot peening can be used to improve fatigue life by deactivating the underlying metallurgical inclusions and substituting a known defect distribution, in the form of shot peening defects, from which cracks grow slowly in the strain hardening layer.
the fatigue crack initiation and growth behaviour in the shot peened condition is controlled by the shot peened defects, rather than the original metallurgical defects.

“In the absence of surface defects, fatigue crack initiation and growth is dominated by the extent of compressive residual stresses and depth of plastic deformation arising from a shot peening process”.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the three-dimensional morphology and the role of inclusions and stringers on fatigue crack initiation and growth in steam turbine blade material, both in a polished and shot peen conditions.

the study of fatigue cracks in the steam turbine blade material, which is tempered martensite with a high volume fraction of non-metallic inclusions (aluminium oxide, manganese sulphide and silicon carbide).
understanding the three dimensional nature of the crack growth process and its interaction with the microstructure and the surface treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a beneficial shot peening treatment can lead to an increase in the fatigue strength of the material in bending, but only if the shot peening treatment is severe enough to produce a sufficiently large compressive residual stress in the surface layer.

shot peening has the effect of changing the crack initiation and growth behaviour from that observed in a polished condition, and that this effect is more pronounced with more intense shot peening conditions.
the shot peened condition is not necessarily the most beneficial in terms of fatigue crack growth rate in the steam turbine blade alloy.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the shot peening condition should be optimised for a particular application and the fatigue crack behaviour should be studied using both serial sectioning as well as CT techniques to fully understand the complex fatigue crack behaviour in this material.
shot peening can provide a significant benefit to fatigue life if a sufficiently severe condition is used, and the surface condition is maintained during the life of the component.
a shot peening process can be used to control the defect population in this type of material.
The main takeaway from our work is that

shot peening is a very effective way to change the fatigue behaviour of a material, even when it is applied to a material that has been designed to be fatigue resistant, such as a turbine blade material.
the fatigue crack initiation and propagation behaviour of a component can be significantly altered by shot peening and the effect is strongly related to the intensity of the shot peening treatment.
shot peening can provide a different defect distribution to the one present in the base material.
